finalText:
**Merge** takes two branches and joins them together, keeping both paths in your history. Everyone can see both lines of work happened side by side. It's safe and honest about what you did.

**Rebase** takes your changes and replays them on top of the other branch, as if you had started from a newer point. The history becomes a single clean line, but you're rewriting when your work happened.

**When to merge:** When the work is done and the branches deserve to stay visible as separate paths. Use it on main when pulling in a feature branch — the merge commit itself documents that the feature landed. Use it when you want to be safe and keep the real history intact.

**When to rebase:** When you want a clean line before you push, or when you're syncing your branch with changes everyone else made. Rebase your feature branch on top of main before the merge — it makes the final history linear and easier to read. Also rebase interactive commits when you're still working locally and want to clean up your message or combine related changes.

The rule of thumb: **rebase locally to keep your work tidy while you're building, then merge to main to document what landed**. Never rebase commits you've pushed and shared — other people's branches might depend on the old version, and you'll create conflicts.
